hall.name: The village hall
hall.text: Trestle tables under bunting, the marrows in a row, the smell of stewed tea. At twenty to two the judges unlocked the committee room to judge the jams, and found that the damson jar entered by Mr Okafor's daughter, nine years old and very proud of it, had been scraped clean with a spoon. All five judges are here, and all five are being very polite to each other. Mr Pask is standing by the marrows with his arms folded.

committee.name: The committee room door
committee.text: A small room with one window and one lock. The jams sit in a row on a cloth, with one empty jar in the middle. A card is pinned to the door in Hen's handwriting.

kitchen.name: The kitchen
kitchen.text: The big urn ticks on the counter. Bernard, who is eighty-one, is pouring tea for a queue and not looking up. The urn rota is taped to the fridge.

stage.name: The stage
stage.text: Lorna, who is nineteen and on the committee because nobody else under sixty would do it, is sorting entry cards into piles and scrolling through her phone.

carpark.name: The car park
carpark.text: Gravel, drizzle, a hatchback with its boot open. The vicar is loading folding chairs into it, one at a time, carefully.

cloakroom.name: The cloakroom
cloakroom.text: Coats on pegs, smelling of rain. Mrs Adeyemi's raincoat, Bernard's anorak, Lorna's denim jacket, and a tweed jacket with something heavy in one pocket.

keys.title: Who has a key
keys.text: KEYS TO THIS ROOM: Mr Pask, Hen, Bernard. NOBODY ELSE. (The jams were locked in here at half past twelve.)

rota.title: The urn rota
rota.text: 1:00 to 1:45, tea urn: BERNARD. And underneath, in different pens: "Bernard never leaves the urn." "Can confirm." "He really doesn't."

photo.title: Lorna's photo
photo.text: Lorna shows you a photo on her phone of the jam table, taken through the committee room window at 1:15. The damson jar is full.

walk.title: The vicar's walk
walk.text: The vicar says Hen was at the post office until half past one (she runs it, and Saturday is busy), then walked back up the hill with him, and they came in together at a quarter to two.

spoon.title: A sticky teaspoon
spoon.text: In the pocket of the tweed jacket (Mr Pask's) is a teaspoon with damson on it. Mr Pask says anyone could have put it there. He's right: on its own, it proves nothing.

chutney.title: Mr Pask's theory
chutney.text: Mr Pask says, without being asked, that you should look at Mrs Adeyemi. "Ask her about the chutney. 2011." He won't say what happened with the chutney. It is a story, not evidence, and it rules nobody out.
